prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 785px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 784px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact order or fulfillment table showing item details, amounts, warehouse locations and tracking identifiers.","reading":"Readers scan across a row to check an item and its fulfillment details, and down columns to compare quantities, prices and totals.","groups":["ID and SKU identify each line item.","Color and Size describe the item variant.","Qty, Price, Tax and Total describe the quantity and monetary amounts.","Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment."],"keep_intact":["Tracking identifiers and numeric values","Column headers and individual words","SKU and warehouse codes where space permits"],"may_wrap":["SKUs at hyphens","Warehouse locations at hyphens; their wrapping can share row height with wrapped SKUs"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [38, 120, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 103, 180] · table 785×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [38, 112, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 111, 180] · table 785×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
